newsitem.title: UK: FORECASTS - UK composites to mirror industry woes.
newsitem.headline: FORECASTS - UK composites to mirror industry woes.

text.p: The corporate reporting season in the insurance industry moves up a gear next week with the first large composites reporting results, Guardian Royal Exchange (GRE) on Tuesday and Commercial Union on Wednesday.
The environment remains difficult for the composites with the recent strength in sterling adding to the industry's dificulties.
Operating profits are expected to fall across the sector, although these declines may be partially offset by an increase in realised investment gains.
Most of the blame for that can be placed on the underlying downturn in the UK market which is suffering the consequences of several years of soft pricing.
In the UK there continues to be significant pressure on commercial lines while overseas, non-life results in most European markets are coming under cyclical pressure, say analysts.
The picture in N.America picture remains more mixed.

Consolidation within the industry has been a theme recently amid speculation that companies may try to offset the weak rating environment by looking for economies of scale and cost savings through defensive mergers.
As the smallest of the composites, GRE has been at the centre of rumours of industry consolidation.
Consensus profit forecasts for GRE of 280 million pounds compare with 1995 results of 340 million pounds. The dividend is expected to rise 11 percent to 10 pence per share.
First half results were well received by the market and while trading profits declined, the results were nevertheless ahead of analyst forecasts.
The company has targeted costs within its UK operations which is expected to continue to be a focus.

In December the group announced 350 jobs were to go in a shake-up of its area and branch network following the 48 million pound acquisition of Legal & General's commercial insurance operations in July.
Commercial Union profits are also expected to decline, with consensus forecasts of 480 million pounds. That compares with last year's pre-tax operating profits of 509 million pounds.
The dividend is forecast to rise to 30.3 pence per share from 28.25 pence.
The sector's major overseas earner, the company is seen as particularly vulnerable to sterling.
The company has significant exposure to France and Holland in terms of both life and non-life premium income.
That currency exposure may take the edge off the contribution from overseas life operations.
"I'm a little bit doubtful whether the market has taken on board the effect of sterling on CU's life profits," said one analyst.
"One reason for investing in CU is that as general insurance turns down it has a growing stream of overseas life profits. I think the market may be surprised by the impact sterling has had on those."
Third quarter operating profits were down nine percent and the company commented then that the rating environment remained competitive.
It was keen to stress then that profitability continues to be emphasised over market share.
While first half results were hit by weather related losses, analysts said that companies wouldn't be able to blame that in the second half.

"For the year as a whole weather losses will probably be broadly similar to last year. Any downturn in results will very much be due to the underlying deterioration in rates that's coming through," said one analyst.
